chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us; he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to me; he said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated to me; he said: Ahmad ibn al-Harith al-Anmati narrated to me, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
When the Qa'im (the Rising One) rises, he will recite this verse,
So I fled from you when I feared you, and my Lord granted me wisdom and made me one of the messengers.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Rising One, a title for the awaited Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.الْمُرْسَلِينَ: The Messengers, referring to those divinely appointed to convey God's message
key_terms.حُكْمًا: Wisdom/Judgment, referring to divine knowledge and authority granted by God

ai.seo_question: What Quranic verse will the Imam al-Qa'im recite upon his rise?
ai.summary: In Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration links the rise of the Twelfth Imam to the Quranic archetype of Prophet Hud, emphasizing that his authority is not merely political but a continuation of prophetic wisdom (*hukm*) granted by God. This connection underscores the Shia belief in the Imam’s divine appointment (*nass*) and his role as the ultimate interpreter of revelation, mirroring the prophetic mission of guidance and deliverance from corruption.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (11) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Suma’a from Ahmad bin al-Harith al-Anmati from al-Mufadhdhal bin Umar that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:
“When al-Qa’im (as) rises, he will recite this Qur’anic verse,
“So I fled from you when I feared you.”
